Bloomberg: Via trade press, citing a person familiar with the plans: FHFA plans to direct the GSEs to shift from three credit reports to two, expected to take effect one to three months after it is announced. No FHFA confirmation or order found as of Nov 2.
Freddie Mac: Credit fees no longer differ by the score model a mortgage is delivered with, for mortgages in MBS issued from October 1.
UWM (UWMC): About 25% of its borrowers get a better result with VantageScore, which it says could reach 40%.
FHFA: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac move to one pricing grid; separate grids make "zero sense," Director Pulte said.

National Mortgage News: Reasons lenders hold back: VantageScore's history does not reach the financial crisis, and lenders risk investor buyback requests if loans underperform. TransUnion extended its 99-cent price through 2028.

Rocket (RKT): VantageScore becomes the default in Q4 on eligible direct-to-consumer loans, including GSE and VA. For now, investment, second-home, FHA, jumbo, home equity and some other loans stay on FICO. Rocket Pro will provide brokers both scores. Has obtained 1.4 million reports with both scores this year. Borrowers who saved with VantageScore saved $1,600 on average at closing. The release does not say it stops ordering FICO.
Milliman: VantageScore loans at Rocket and UWM, May to August, carried rates about 9.3 bp above comparable FICO loans. The authors cannot identify the driver and say the gap may narrow.

Equifax and TransUnion: Via trade press. Both now sell a mortgage credit file with one score or none and let a lender add a score later. The article does not say which score to buy first. Equifax charges $1 plus the score for a repull within 24 hours. With TransUnion, a lender adding a score does not pay for a second report when conditions are met.

PennyMac: Can now handle both scores on bulk conforming loans. On Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac loans it no longer requires a Classic FICO or a credit report with both scores, while still recommending both. A VantageScore-only bid enters 0 in the FICO field. VA, FHA, USDA and non-agency products still need Classic FICO.

FHA: Mortgagee Letter 2026-11 adds VantageScore 4.0 and FICO 10T beside Classic FICO on Title II programs, for case numbers assigned on or after January 1, 2027. Three credit reports and the existing score floors stay. A lender may submit one model or several; if several, the lowest score counts. The report kept in the file may hold models not submitted.

Equifax (EFX): Nearly 2,000 mortgage lenders and resellers took a free VantageScore 4.0 score with a paid legacy score from April through September. More than 165 lenders use VantageScore 4.0 alone at $1 for certain loan types.
UWM (UWMC): Dropped its own minimum credit scores on Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and Ginnie Mae loans, effective at once; non-agency products keep them. Scores still set pricing.
FICO: Says UWM reaffirmed it will use FICO on all credit pulls across its broker lending, alongside other eligible models.
UWM (UWMC): Now pulls both scores on every report and automatically uses the stronger result, so brokers no longer choose.

FICO: Holds its wholesale mortgage price at $10, flat on the year, for lenders and brokers enrolled in its Preferred Program through participating tri-merge resellers. The $10 buys a bundle of Classic FICO and FICO 10T. The release asks for a commitment to FICO and states no terms, no end date and no price for anyone else.

Mark Begor, Equifax CEO: Says the price gap, about $1 against $10 or more, is what will drive VantageScore adoption, and expects buying VantageScore first and FICO later to be the exception. VantageScore's site calls it a joint venture of Equifax, Experian and TransUnion.

Equifax (EFX): Says about 2,000 mortgage lenders use VantageScore in underwriting, up sevenfold since April. Its Oct 8 release counts nearly 2,000 lenders and resellers taking a free VantageScore with a paid legacy score. That count does not show use in a credit decision. Most lenders still buy FICO. More than 200, which Equifax calls smaller, use VantageScore alone. Holds a $1 price through 2028. Full conversion to VantageScore would add about $35 million of margin. Q4 guidance assumes FICO on all mortgage transactions.

FICO: Says Fairway, Movement and Rate enrolled in its Preferred Program, its $10 bundle, and will keep pulling FICO across their mortgage lending. The release states no price or terms. None of the lenders' own quotes mentions enrolling: Movement's says it will keep pulling FICO, Fairway's that it will keep evaluating FICO. National Mortgage News adds that lenders still report a need for both FICO and VantageScore.

CrossCountry: Its release says the first 60 days of using VantageScore 4.0 saved an estimated average of $2,500 a loan, from preliminary internal data, counting only loans where it gave a better score. National Mortgage News calls that a 60-day test and quotes it saying VantageScore is not yet accepted in all programs.

HousingWire: Mostly from unnamed sources: FICO is preparing a flat-fee annual subscription for 2027, priced on a lender's past volume, beside its Preferred Program. One source says existing clients have until January 31 to choose a path. FICO did not immediately respond.

Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac: Each reported VantageScore 4.0 at about 6% of its Q3 acquisitions and about 2% of its first nine months (a footnote in Fannie's Oct 28 10-Q, a table in Freddie's Oct 29 10-Q). Each is on that GSE's own basis, not by issue month. Freddie says adopting VantageScore 4.0 and one grid could change the loans it buys and lower the guarantee fees it receives on new loans.

Rocket (RKT): Q3 results: says that in September it became the first mortgage lender to adopt VantageScore 4.0 as its preferred model on all eligible loans. Coverage of the earnings call shows no discussion of it.

Sandra Thompson: The former FHFA director questions putting Classic FICO and VantageScore on one LLPA grid, since the same number from two models may not carry the same risk, and asks to see the analysis behind it.

TransUnion (TRU): About 35% of mortgage credit pulls in Q3 used VantageScore 4.0. Its Jul 28 slides put VantageScore in about 30% of pulls. Its slides do not say whose pulls; we take them as its own. A pull that includes the score is not a loan priced on it. Mortgage inquiries fell about 16% on the year in Q3 and are guided down 20% or more in Q4.

Fannie Mae: Fannie's credit score page, which carries no date, says 37% of conventional applications created in Desktop Underwriter in September 2026 included a VantageScore 4.0 score. An application that includes the score is not a loan priced on it.

FHFA: Director Pulte wrote that FHFA is taking more action that week so that score competition is real. National Mortgage News adds that he has hinted he may allow alternatives to three credit reports. FICO shares fell about 13% that day, the first trading day after its $10 hold. No formal FHFA step found as of Nov 2.

Mizuho and UBS: Via trade press, not their notes. Enrolled lenders are reported to pull FICO on every application, soft and hard, with VantageScore added, not swapped in. Mizuho says this blunts buying VantageScore first and moved its 2027 FICO price growth from about 5% to flat. UBS says the $10 leaves out funding, closed-loan and success fees and starts on enrollment.

rows.text: FICO: Reports mortgage origination revenue of $241 million for the quarter to Sep 30, 2026, 58% of its Scores revenue: up 72% on the year on a higher price per score, with volumes down by high single digits, and below the quarter before's $282 million on lower volume and more home equity at a lower price. Gives no fiscal 2027 guidance, citing its move to lender-by-lender mortgage pricing for 2027 and uncertain mortgage-market conditions. Its CEO says lenders enrolled in its Preferred Program get no 2027 wholesale price increase, the program is not exclusive, and FICO will no longer disclose its other prices or terms. Its slides list UWM first among the program's announced participants.
FICO: Names DHI Mortgage, loanDepot, Paramount Residential Mortgage Group and CMG Financial as enrolled in its Preferred Program. It says it will not name every participant.

UWM (UWMC): Extends VantageScore to select non-agency loans: jumbo, bank statement, Investor Flex, doctor, HELOC and home equity. Per trade press, its system still obtains both FICO and VantageScore and uses the higher, and non-agency lenders and investors keep their own score rules. Its page also lists VA and FHA Streamlines as open to VantageScore.
FICO: Names Guild Mortgage, New American Funding and PennyMac Financial Services as enrolled in its Preferred Program.
